newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS says too soon to assess Ontario restructuring.
newsitem.headline: DBRS says too soon to assess Ontario restructuring.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service on Thursday said it is too early for it to assess the impact of Ontario's plan to restructure the way it finances unicipalities.
As a result, the Toronto-based bond rating agency said it is not taking any rating action with respect to the proposed restructuring.
The bond rating agency said it will be making individual assessments of the municipalities it rates as the restructuring programs become more clearly defined.

Under the Ontario plan, there will be fundamental changes to education, social welfare and housing, the property tax system and other servcies. DBRS said the main risk to municipalities is they will be forced significantly raise property taxes as a result of all the program changes.

However, a support program included in the province's plans could act as an equalization payment system and the fiscal integrity of the municipalities could potentially be sustained, the rating agency said.
"Until the design of the support program funds are more fully detailed, it is not possible to determine the effects of the restructuring individual municipalities," DBRS said.

The rating agency said the issue is further complicated by plans to amalgamate some municipalities. As a result, the agency said it will assess the municipalities it rates as the restructuring programs are more clearly defined.
